cases.prompt: src/retry.py has this field: `attempts = 3  # attempts count`. Improve the comment and name so a first-time reader knows the exact meaning without reading the code.
expectations: The new comment states units/scope precisely: what one 'attempt' is and what the count covers (e.g., retries after the initial try).
The agent does not merely repeat the variable name in the comment.
Boundary semantics are documented (does 3 mean 3 total tries or 3 retries?).
If the name was changed, the new name is more precise (e.g., maxRetries vs attempts).

cases.prompt: In src/client.ts, the method fetchUser(id) has an interface comment that explains it uses a two-phase RPC with an internal retry queue. Move implementation details out of the interface comment and into the body where they belong, keeping the interface comment complete for callers.
expectations: The rewritten interface comment covers behavior, arguments, return value, side effects, and exceptions without internal RPC/retry-queue details.
Implementation narrative is relocated into the method body as implementation comments (what/why, not how).
The agent does not delete information callers need (e.g., blocking behavior, error cases).

cases.prompt: My team writes one comment above every single line of code explaining what it does. They say it makes the code readable. Is that a good practice?
expectations: The agent explains that same-level comments repeat the code and add no information, per the non-obviousness test.
The agent gives the correct alternative: higher-level block comments describing intent, lower-level comments adding precision where code can't.
The agent does not endorse line-per-line commenting.
